drivingQuestion: Why is the poor person liable, given that lifting and placing require a surface four by four handbreadths and a hand lacks that size?
outcomeNote: The unit contains only the question; its resolution lies in the following unit.

segments.he: פָּשַׁט הֶעָנִי אֶת יָדוֹ: אַמַּאי חַיָּיב? וְהָא בָּעֵינַן עֲקִירָה וְהַנָּחָה מֵעַל גַּבֵּי מְקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה, וְלֵיכָּא?
segments.en: We learned in the mishna several examples where «the poor person extended his hand:» One, when he placed an object into the hand of the homeowner and one, when he took an object from the hand of the homeowner. In those cases, we learned that he is liable to bring a sin-offering. The Gemara asks: «Why is he liable? Don’t we require» that halakhic «lifting and placing» be performed «from» and onto «the surface of an area» that is «four by four» handbreadths? A smaller area is not considered a defined place, and it is as if the object were not there at all; «and» a person’s hand «is not» that size. Why, then, is he liable?
